about.title: La Canada Flintridge Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases are different from most personal injury claims, and that's especially true here in La Canada Flintridge, where patients often travel to nearby Glendale, Pasadena, or Los Angeles-area facilities for specialty care. California law under MICRA sets tight rules: a short window to act, a required pre-suit notice, and a cap on certain damages. Because of that, timing and documentation matter from day one. A bad result during treatment doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred — proving a claim usually requires a qualified medical expert who can speak to whether the standard of care was actually breached. We listen to what happened, review your medical records, and explain in plain terms whether you may have a case worth pursuing. There's no charge unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Details Matter in These Claims

items.title: Short, Strict Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the date of injury, to bring a claim. Missing that window can end a case regardless of its merits.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can be filed, California law typically requires sending the healthcare provider written notice at least 90 days in advance. We can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: A negative outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — California courts generally require a qualified medical expert to confirm the standard of care was breached and caused harm.

items.question: I live in La Canada Flintridge but was treated at a hospital in another city — does that matter?
items.answer: Malpractice claims are usually based on where the treatment happened and which providers were involved, not where you live. We review your case based on the medical records regardless of the hospital's location.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having your timeline reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California law caps certain non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap. We can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves risk, and not every poor result is the result of an error. Malpractice generally requires showing the provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that failure caused harm.
